problemStatement.formal: axiom steinerberger_criterion (n p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hp_le : p ≤ n) (hleading : leadingDigit n p = p - 1) : p ∣ harmonicGCD n
problemStatement.plain: Let n ≥ 1, L_n = lcm{1,...,n}, and define a_n by H_n = a_n / L_n. Do both gcd(a_n, L_n) = 1 and gcd(a_n, L_n) > 1 occur for infinitely many n?
whyMatters: Connects harmonic number arithmetic to prime factorization of lcm
Part 2 proved via Steinerberger/Wolstenholme, Part 1 remains OPEN
Related to Schanuel's conjecture and transcendence theory

proven: L_pos, L_dvd_factorial, dvd_L: structural L properties
H_pos, H_strict_mono, H_mono: structural H properties
small_examples: gcd values for n=1..6 (gcd=1 for n<=5, gcd=3 for n=6)
part2_trivially_true: infinitely many n with gcd > 1 (via {2*3^k})
Leading digit properties and concrete computations
open: Part 1: infinitely many n with gcd(a_n, L_n) = 1 (OPEN)
